text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm planning a small infra change: migrate model-level feature flags from a ConfigMap to a Secret so we can use KMS encryption and tighter RBAC. Drafting a Terraform change that creates `kubernetes_secret.model_flags` and updates the deployment mounts. Want quick ops/infra + runtime sanity checks before I open the PR.

aj: Quick q — are we changing how the app reads the flags (env vs mounted file)? runtime currently expects a mounted JSON file from the ConfigMap.

maria: Good point. Plan is to keep the same mount path and filename so runtime sees no config change. The Secret will contain the same JSON payload, base64-encoded. Terraform will swap the `kubernetes_config_map` -> `kubernetes_secret` resource and update the `volume` block to `secret { secret_name = ... }`.

kevin: That should be fine but watch permissions: service account needs `get`/`watch` on secrets in the ns. Also projected volumes might be better if you want to combine configmap + secret later.

aj: If we keep the mount path identical, runtime shouldn't care. But runtime code has a fallback that logs a WARN if it can't parse flags; can we add a quick smoke check in the rollout to validate parsing?

maria: Yeah I'll add a post-deploy smoke job that `curl localhost:8080/health && cat /etc/flags/flags.json | jq .` and fail if invalid.

sahil: Security note — make sure to add `kms_key_id` on the secret creation path (we store secrets in KMS). Also we should not leak the base64 in TF state — use `sops`/conventions or use secret ref to KMS.

maria: Thanks. My draft uses `data = { flags = base64encode(file("${path.module}/flags.json")) }` which will put the secret value into state. I can switch to `kubectl`-managed secret via a migration job instead so Terraform doesn't hold plaintext. Thoughts?

kevin: I prefer migration job approach — TF creates an empty secret resource (placeholder) then a k8s Job copies the CM -> Secret with `kubectl create secret generic model-flags --from-file=... --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -` then TF can adopt. Prevents sensitive data in TF state.

aj: Sounds good. For rollout strategy: canary 10% for 5m then full. Runtime team can look at logs for parsing errors. I'll hook up a quick alert if `flags.parse_errors > 0` during canary. :eyes: 

maria: I'll put the PR up with: 1) migration Job manifest 2) TF placeholder secret + adoption notes 3) updated deployment volume to secret 4) smoke job and canary rollout config. Will tag runtime/eng-sre for verification.

deploy-bot: deploy-checklist: lint terraform (tfsec ok), k8s manifests validated (kubeval), no image changes.

sahil: Also add an audit note about retention and access — compliance will want to see KMS usage and who can patch the secret.

maria: Will add. PR should be ready for review by EOD. If anyone wants early look lemme know and I'll share the branch.

aj: I can review the runtime piece tomorrow morning.

kevin: Happy to review infra/Terraform.

maria: Thanks — tagging both you in the PR when it's up.
